facts.text: The served model is the MJCF gripper model conda/robotiq_gripper_85.xml, whose root element is '<mujoco model="robotiq_gripper_85_model">'
The model declares two <position> actuators, finger_1 on joint finger_joint and finger_2 on joint right_outer_knuckle_joint, each with ctrllimited true and ctrlrange 0 0.85
finger_joint is a hinge with range 0 to 0.872664626 rad
left_inner_finger_joint is a hinge with range -0.8757 to 0.8757 rad
left_inner_knuckle_joint is a hinge with range 0 to 0.8757 rad
right_outer_knuckle_joint is a hinge with range 0 to 0.872664626 rad
right_inner_finger_joint is a hinge with range -0.8757 to 0.8757 rad
right_inner_knuckle_joint is a hinge with range 0 to 0.8757 rad
Two fixed tendons couple finger_joint with the left inner joints and right_outer_knuckle_joint with the right inner joints, with coefficients 1, -3 and 1
The model declares a force sensor and a torque sensor at the site ft_frame
The model's <asset> block declares the STL meshes of the gripper under meshes/robotiq_85_gripper/
The conda gripper class loads the MJCF through robosuite's xml_path_completion('grippers/robotiq_gripper_85.xml')
The conda setup copies robotiq_gripper_85.xml into robosuite's models/assets/grippers directory
The binary gripper variant maps a continuous action to binary output: -1 means open and 1 means closed
The binary gripper variant clips current_action to -1.0 to 1.0
TabletopEnv is located in environment/tabletop_env.py and inherits robosuite's SingleArmEnv
The documented primitive actions of the environment include open_gripper and close_gripper
The environment starts the gripper at current_action [-1.0] (open)
The environment reports the gripper closed when current_action exceeds 0.9
MuBlE is a MuJoCo and Blender simulation environment for task planning in robotics manipulation

determinism.notes: MuJoCo integrates one model deterministically from one initial state; the bridge takes no seed input and cap.world.reset.v1 restores the model defaults, so a run repeats on the same engine but no seed selects a different state; the stand-in integrates its own placeholder motion

gaps: the fake backend is a stand-in for the mujoco library, not MuJoCo: it reads the model text for the joint count, the actuator count and the control ranges but integrates a placeholder first-order motion of each actuated joint toward its control target, so contacts, tendon coupling and actuator dynamics are not MuJoCo's
the stand-in loads no mesh or texture and resolves no contact, equality or tendon constraint; the two fixed tendons of the model are not applied

the model's <asset> block names STL meshes under meshes/robotiq_85_gripper/ that are not present in the clone, so the real mujoco backend can resolve them only from an installed robosuite asset tree; the fake needs none of them
MuJoCo itself was not importable where the gate ran, so no trajectory of this package was compared with the real engine
no rendering is offered and no physical gripper is modelled; nothing was validated against the Robotiq 2F-85 hardware
